newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT-Salomon upgrades Asian fibre makers.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Salomon upgrades Asian fibre makers.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said in a recent research report Asia Pacific Oils and Chemicals Quarterly Report that investors should move downstream to producers who are net buyers of upstream raw materials.
"We believe there is limited downside to earnings for downstream producers who are net buyers of petrochemical raw materials," said analyst Janet Yang.
"Our favoured polyester stocks include Far Eastern Textile and Nan Ya Plastics Corp of Taiwan, PT Indorama Synthetics of Indonesia and Yizheng Chemical Fibre Co Ltd of China."
Salomon rates these stocks as buys.

Although Yizheng Chemical's two main products, polyester fibre chips and staple fibres, have been slower to recover in China during the first half of this year, there are signs that Chinese textile exports have picked up 35 percent year to year from the fall in 1995, said Yang.
This bodes well for the polyester industry and Yizheng, said Yang.

"Indorama Synthetics has just completed its major capacity expansion and we expect the company to announce its next strategic move shortly," said Yang. "Our 12-month target price for the share is 2,500 rupiah."

Nan Ya Plastics has substantial exposure to investments such as the sixth naptha cracker project. Phase I is scheduled to start up in 1998, which is expected to provide significant earnings upside, the report said.
Salomon is forecasting earnings per share of NT$3.13, higher than the consensus 1997 forecast of NT$2.95.
"High operating leverage and significant exposure to downstream products should enable FET (Far Eastern Textile) to double its earnings in 1997," Yang said.
Growth in earnings of the company's 62.4 percent held Far East Tone, a mobile telephone operating company, will be the main driver of non-operating income, the report said.
Salomon has a six-month target price of NT$53 for FET.
